cap: In postmenopausal bleeding, first look at the vulva, vagina and cervix, then sample the lining with an office endometrial biopsy, the first test. Hysteroscopy gives a direct view and targeted samples, and dilation and curettage scrapes the lining when the office sample is inadequate. Benign causes include polyps, acute endometritis, chronic endometritis with plasma cells, and Asherman syndrome, scarring of the basalis after curettage.
